thread:
Nadia: Starting cross-shard metadata_migration on prod now. Plan: add nullable metadata_v2, backfill in shard batches of 500, 150 qps, 90m window. Will watch locks and tail latency. @Ravi @Jo please ack.

deploy-bot: Job 8123 queued: metadata_migration:v2 -> prod (shard-01). Logs: https://ci/reports/8123

Ravi: Ack. Suggest we set a DB circuit-breaker flag so the job can be gracefully stopped on lock pressure.

Jo: +1. Also can we pin backend to release 4.0.6 for the duration? The schema access changed in 4.1.

Nadia: Yes — pin backend to 4.0.6 for the run. Rollback window is 25m after each shard wave.

deploy-bot: Shard-01 wave started (500 rows). Estimated duration 8m.

ops-bot: Metric spike: row-level lock waits increased 2.9x on shard-01. Top query: UPDATE accounts SET metadata_v2 = ... WHERE id IN (...)
Waiters: 37, avg wait 1.4s.

Luis: Observed 95th tail latency bump on account read path, error rate up from 0.08% to 0.6% for 90s.

Nadia: Hitting the circuit-breaker: pausing remaining shards. Do not start shard-02.

Ravi: Initiating graceful stop and snapshot. deploy-bot, cancel job 8123 and save progress.

deploy-bot: Cancel acknowledged. Snapshot saved -> s3://migrations/8123-snapshot-1751112222.tar.gz.

Jo: Pin applied: kubectl set image deploy/backend backend=registry/backend:4.0.6 -n prod.

Nadia: Decision: abort this iteration. We’ll rework to use a streaming backfill with per-connection limit and a DB-level statement_timeout. Also adding a soft-locking helper (SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED).

Luis: Recommend we add a temporary read-fallback that serves legacy metadata when metadata_v2 is null to avoid user-facing regressions.

Ravi: I'll draft the rollback playbook and a runbook for the circuit-breaker toggles. Also schedule a canary run on staging with streaming approach.

Nadia: Action items: Ravi -> runbook + canary; Jo -> release pin + release-note bullet; Luis -> read-fallback patch; Me -> update migration job to streaming + SKIP LOCKED. Reopen thread after canary. :memo:
